01 / OVERVIEW

From weapon motion
to material response.

The study follows one impact through detection, evaluation and presentation. Reusable weapon and material presets keep the calculations separate from the authored response.

  1. 01Weapon motion
  2. 02Collision
  3. 03Impact solver
  4. 04Impact data
  5. 05Deformation / VFX

Conceptual pipeline. In the implementation, deformation is called directly; the event payload feeds VFX and Debug observers.

02 / SELECTED TECHNICAL HIGHLIGHTS

Detection, evaluation
and response.

01 / Motion & collision

Track the contact region

A SphereCast sweeps the detection point’s travelled segment during an animation-driven attack window. A collider is processed once per swing.

Contact area and sweep radius are separate controls, so pressure tuning does not change collision thickness.

02 / Impact solver

Evaluate before presenting

Alignment, hardness and pressure classify each hit. The strength input is mass × velocity: a momentum-inspired control value for the authored response.

“Penetrated” is a result label; the system does not cut or fracture the mesh.

03 / Shader Graph

Localize and release the deformation

Material hardness and elasticity scale the displacement. Spatial falloff localizes it, while hold time, damped oscillation and reduced rebound control its recovery.

A MaterialPropertyBlock supplies per-object parameters. The frozen implementation uses contact area directly as the visual radius.

04 / Data & presentation

Share the evaluated impact

ScriptableObjects hold weapon and material presets. A common ImpactData event feeds VFX and Debug observers; deformation is called directly on the receiver.

Each material selects its particle prefab. Effects face the surface normal, with a small downward spawn offset.

03 / COMPARISONS

Material and weapon
comparisons.

Final Showcase frames compare authored responses rather than controlled physical measurements.

Slime

Indentation + droplets

A local depression recovers as blue droplets leave the surface.

Stone

Brittle debris

Separate mesh particles burst away; the target remains intact.

Metal

Brief sparks

Stretched spark streaks mark contact with the hard-surface target.

Changing the weapon

Hammer, sword and spear strike Slime with different motion and weapon settings. The localized response follows each recorded contact.

04 / PROBLEMS, ITERATIONS & PERFORMANCE

Iteration and performance.

01

Contact area ≠ collision radius

Splitting the two controls corrected early contact on broad weapons without changing the pressure model.

02

Geometry is part of the shader

Slime’s topology and normals were revised to address faceting and uneven highlights during development.

03

A clearer third material

Carapace became Metal so the target and spark effect expressed the same material idea.

Supporting evidence / Runtime debugging +

The Debug Panel observes the same impact event as the VFX manager. It shows evaluated data for one recorded impact and is not a profiler. Solver deformation force is an intermediate value that ImpactReceiver scales again before passing it to the shader.

05 / SCOPE, SOURCES & CREDITS

Scope, sources and credits.

This is a material-response study, not a complete combat or destruction system. Displacement affects rendered vertices, without changing topology or collision geometry. A single swept detection point approximates the weapon’s contact region.

The implementation is frozen. Effects are instantiated per impact; deformation stores one hit at a time. No performance benchmark is claimed.
